Hi Tim — thanks for the heads up and the calendar.

Short answer: we cannot guarantee the standard 15-minute P1 first response for the full 4h maintenance window if routing from eu-west-1 is degraded — some alerts will hit our regional frontends and some may queue during retries. That said, we can offer a controlled mitigation and an official, temporary SLA amendment you can present to your compliance team.

Proposed mitigation (subject to internal approvals):
- Temporary P1 first-response window: 45 minutes (instead of 15) during the 02:00–06:00 UTC window on Nov 10 for incidents caused by the maintenance.
- Escalation path: primary on-call (karthik_iyer) -> secondary on-call (marcus_lin) -> on-call lead (marissa_cole). We will create a dedicated bridge channel for this maintenance and enable high-priority page routing to the EU on-call.
- Technical fallback: enable read-only traffic routing to global replicas for affected tenants where applicable; Marcus will confirm capacity and KV cache warmup plan.
- Commercial remediation: a one-time standby credit to the invoice for November (TBD percent) if we confirm measurable customer impact caused by the maintenance.

I've attached a populated SLA exception request form for internal sign-off (sla_exception_request_form.pdf) and the maintenance ICS you sent. Can Karthik and Marcus confirm feasibility (capacity + on-call coverage) and suggest a recommended percentage credit? If internal approvals are OK, I'll send you a formal amendment and the escalation contacts to share with your ops/compliance team.

Thanks — Laura
Laura Bennett
